scope: Adapter3 private Linux synthetic qualification: full-handler admission drain/resume, exact original/final dispatch constraints with attributed durable errors, native protocol scope, owning-parent lifetime, legacy-format journal checkpoint replay and recovered-copy continuation; plus established protocol, durability, inspector and authentication regressions. Installation, real providers and full Host backup/restore remain separate.
networkIsolation: all final process qualification commands ran inside private user/network namespaces with loopback only
notes: No installed service, existing account credentials or default product ports were operated.
The exact upstream v8.0.41 archive and existing two patch files remain unchanged.

The pinned SDK attempts a public npm client-version metadata check at startup; the final private-network qualification prevents that lookup reaching any external network. This upstream behavior was not disabled in production by these changes.
Parent EOF/owner death now exits cleanly; unknown usage after an abrupt Core kill remains explicit rather than invented.
Sparse indexing preserves the flat journal/source/cursor format; actual old-binary rollback was not tested. No automatic deletion or recovery-copy adoption is performed.
Complete configuration/credential-generation/journal/SQLite backup restoration and sustained production growth remain unqualified by these checks.
